title: Anthropometric accommodation (definition)
text: Having sufficient reach, movement, clearance, and visibility to safely perform all required tasks while wearing the appropriate mission ensemble and equipment; includes clearance for movement, ingress/egress of work areas, internal and external visibility, and reach and actuation of controls through their full range of travel.
site_hook: Defines the four checks the site should run per task: reach, clearance, visibility, ingress/egress.

title: Central 90 percent accommodation (definition)
text: Multivariate central 90 percent of suitably clothed and equipped males and of females; the 10 percent not accommodated should be split evenly between the small and large ends; multivariate methods are required when several measures must be accommodated at once; univariate accommodation can use the 5th to 95th percentiles of a single dimension.
site_hook: Univariate: P5..P95 of the governing dimension per sex. Multivariate: count ANSUR II individuals (and other open datasets) that pass all relevant dimension checks at once.
percentile_rule: 5th-95th per sex (univariate); multivariate central 90% per sex otherwise

title: Accommodation (general rule)
limits: accommodated fraction per sex: >= 90 (preferred 95) % [males and females separately]
text: Unless otherwise specified, equipment, systems and subsystems shall accommodate the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped females of the target user population.
site_hook: Default boundary for every anthropometric check: P5 female .. P95 male (univariate) or multivariate 90% per sex; 'preferred' level P2.5..P97.5.
percentile_rule: central 90% (95% preferred) of males AND of females

title: Accommodation rule (general)
limits: accommodated fraction of males (multivariate central): >= 90 (preferred 95) % [suitably clothed and equipped] | accommodated fraction of females (multivariate central): >= 90 (preferred 95) % [suitably clothed and equipped]
text: Unless otherwise specified elsewhere in this standard or by the procuring activity, equipment, systems, and subsystems shall be designed to accommodate both the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males of the target user population, and the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped females of the target user population.
site_hook: Global compliance rule: run every geometric check for a mannequin family spanning the central 90% (95% preferred) of each sex; site can approximate with P5F..P95M (or P2.5F..P97.5M) univariate cases, better with a multivariate boundary-case set (e.g. PCA ellipse cases from ANSUR II) plus clothing/equipment increments
percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of males and of females, clothed and equipped

title: Design factors: space, access, clothing compatibility
text: Design should reflect, when applicable: (d) space for personnel, their equipment, and free volume for movements during operation and maintenance under normal, adverse, and emergency conditions; (i) passageways, hatches, ladders, stairways, platforms, inclines and other provisions for ingress, egress and passage; (j) body support and restraint, seating; (p) compatibility of the design, location and layout of controls, displays, workspaces, maintenance accesses, stowage provisions, passenger compartments and control movements with the clothing and personal equipment to be worn.
site_hook: Checklist; supports adding clothing/equipment increments (helmet, body armour, CBRN, arctic) to mannequin dimensions for clearance checks

title: Crew-served interaction
text: The design of the system shall reflect the interaction requirements of crew-served equipment.
site_hook: Checklist; multi-mannequin scenes could show crew positions

title: Fall protection: elevated work height threshold
limits: elevated work location height threshold: >= 4 ft [general industry] | elevated work location height threshold: >= 5 ft [maritime industry]
text: Design shall provide protection or prevention of falls from elevated work surfaces in accordance with ANSI/ASSP Z359. Design shall limit risk of fall from elevated work locations, considered to be 4 feet in general industry and 5 feet in maritime industry, through a hierarchy of controls (eliminate, fixed barriers such as handrails, aerial lifts/scaffolding, administrative controls). When fixed barriers are not feasible, designs shall provide a personal fall arrest system.
site_hook: Sandbox platform/work surface height: flag fall-protection need (guardrail/handrail object) when standing surface height >= 4 ft (1.22 m) general or 5 ft (1.52 m) maritime

title: Fall protection: anchor points and fall clearance
limits: anchor point test load: >= 5000 lb | total fall clearance (lanyard expansion + person height): (preferred 15) ft [typical value]
text: Fall prevention programs include: (b) certified anchor points (5,000-pound [lb] test) for harnesses in accessible locations; (c) certified full-body harnesses (belts shall not be used except for positioning); (d) fall distance calculation accommodating lanyard expansion plus allowance for height of the person (typically 15 feet [ft] total); (f) anchor points placed so the individual will not pendulum into harm's way.
site_hook: Could check clearance below an elevated platform >= 15 ft (4.57 m) when fall arrest is the control; anchor rating is manual

title: Personal fall arrest system limits
limits: arrest impact force on person: <= 1800 lb | anchorage strength: >= 3600 lb [exclusive (>)]
text: A personal fall arrest system includes an approved full-body harness and equipment providing controlled expansion that limits the impact forces on the victim (to 1,800 pounds) and certified anchorages (> 3,600 lbs).
site_hook: Checklist / info only

title: CBRNE PPE compatibility
text: As applicable, equipment design shall be compatible with CBRNE, directed energy, or other mission-required PPE.
site_hook: Add PPE clothing ensemble option (mask, hood, gloves, overboots) that increments mannequin dimensions and reduces ROM; re-run reach/clearance checks

title: Mission-essential operations in CBRNE PPE
text: Equipment design shall permit performance of mission-essential operations, communications, maintenance, resupply, and decontamination tasks by suitably clothed, trained, and acclimatized personnel for the survival periods and CBRNE environments specified.
site_hook: Checklist; PPE mannequin variant for reach/clearance

title: Anthropometric accommodation of PPE
text: Anthropometric accommodation and design of CBRNE, directed energy protection, or other mission-required PPE systems shall be in accordance with section 5.8.
site_hook: Cross-reference to 5.8 anthropometry; use survey data for PPE sizing
percentile_rule: per 5.8

title: Colour-deficient users
text: Colors used for functional purposes (visual displays, controls, workspaces, equipment connections) shall accommodate users with color-deficient vision.
site_hook: Checklist; optionally simulate colour-deficient view of a display object

title: Aircrew systems
text: Aircrew systems shall be designed as specified (see 6.2). Refer to JSSG-2010 for further guidance; additional aircrew system design guidance in MIL-DTL-7788.
site_hook: Reference only; pilot postures exist but limits come from JSSG-2010

title: Ejection acceleration limits
limits: acceleration exposure duration in scope: <= 1 s [short-duration (less than one second)]
text: For guidance on exposure to short-duration (less than one second), linear and angular acceleration during ejection seat operation, see ADV-PUB-4048. Parachute-opening acceleration after seat separation is excluded.
site_hook: No numeric limit in 1472H; refers to ADV-PUB-4048

title: Crash protection references
text: For occupant crash protection and crash-protective aspects of seating, restraint, crewstation and passenger/troop station design, see JSSG-2010-7 and USAAVSCOM TR 89-D-22 (A through E), Aircraft Crash Survival Design Guide Volumes 1 through 5.
site_hook: Reference only

title: Escape and egress systems
text: For guidance on escape and egress systems, see MIL-HDBK-516.
site_hook: Reference only

title: Selection of mechanical controls (Table I / Table II)
text: Criteria in Table I should be used to choose the best type of mechanical control for control panels; Table II shows recommended controls by control function and actuation force (small vs large).
site_hook: New 'control' sandbox object with a control-type and function parameter; look up Table I preference rank (1/2/3) and Table II recommendation; report as advisory

title: Accommodation of user population (controls and motion envelopes)
limits: accommodated population: >= 90 (preferred 95) % (multivariate central) [males and females separately]
text: Unless otherwise specified, the type of control selected and the location of the motion envelopes shall accommodate the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped females of the target user population for body dimensions.
site_hook: Run reach check of each control object for a boundary set of mannequins (e.g., P5 female and P95 male, or multivariate boundary cases) and report pass/fail per control
percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

title: Two-dimensional design elements: percentiles
limits: strength percentile: >= 5 percentile [strength] | dimension percentile: 5-95 percentile [univariate dimension]
text: Fifth percentile strength values and 5th or 95th percentile univariate physical dimension values shall be used for two-dimensional design elements (see figures 22 and 23).
site_hook: Use P5/P95 single-dimension values from selected survey for 2-D layout checks; P5 strength for force limits
percentile_rule: 5th percentile strength; 5th or 95th percentile univariate dimensions

title: Handedness accommodation
text: Equipment design shall accommodate both right- and left-handed users.
site_hook: Mirror the mannequin (left-hand reach) and re-run reach checks for hand-operated controls

title: Handedness priority
text: If constraints permit only one group of users (right- or left-handed) to be accommodated, the majority of the target user population shall receive priority.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Compatibility with handwear
text: Controls shall be compatible with handwear to be utilized in the anticipated environment. Unless specified for glove use, all dimensions herein are for bare hands and shall be adjusted for use with gloves or mittens (see table VII).
site_hook: Add a 'handwear' parameter (bare/flash glove/heavy glove/arctic mitten) to control checks; apply glove adders from figures/tables

title: Distribution of workload across limbs
text: Controls should be selected and distributed so that none of the user's limbs will be overburdened.
site_hook: Checklist item; could count controls assigned per limb

title: Multirotation controls
text: Multirotation controls should be used when precision is required over a wide range of adjustment.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Detent controls
text: Detent controls shall be selected whenever the operational mode requires control operation in discrete steps.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Stops
text: Stops shall be provided at the beginning and end of the range-of-control positions if the control is not to be operated beyond the indicated end positions or within specified limits.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Power assist feedback
text: Power assist may be used to reduce force inputs. When servo-amplifier devices are used, proportional resistance or force feedback shall be provided to give the feel of unpowered control.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Consistency of movement direction
text: Direction of control movement shall be consistent with related movement of an associated display, equipment component, or vehicle. In general, forward, clockwise, to the right, up, or pressing shall turn on, increase, or move forward/clockwise/right/up. Valve controls excluded.
site_hook: Checklist item; could be a direction attribute on control objects

title: Multidimensional operation exception
text: When the vehicle/equipment may move in more than two dimensions, exception to 5.1.1.2.1 shall be made if needed to ensure consistency of anticipated response (e.g., forward stick causes descent).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Mechanical control criteria (preference by function)
text: Preference ranking (1 = most preferred, 2 = secondary, 3 = least) of selector switch, round knob, discrete thumbwheel, continuous thumbwheel, crank, push button, toggle switch, rocker switch, lever, joystick/lever/ball/mouse for each function. Examples: Select power ON-OFF: push button 1, lever 1a (heavy duty power circuits), toggle 2, rocker 2, selector 3. 3-state OFF-STBY-ON: selector 1, round knob 2, toggle 2, rocker 3. Select one of 3 to 24 discrete alternatives (sequential): selector switch 1. Set value on continuous scale: round knob 1, continuous thumbwheel 2, crank 3, lever 3. Enter alphanumeric data: push button (keyboard) 1. Initiate directional function: toggle 1, rocker 1d, lever 1, push button 2d, joystick/ball/mouse 2. Engage-disengage mechanical function: lever 1. Coarse adjustment: round knob (small diameter) 1; cont. thumbwheel (small motion) 2, crank (few turns) 2, lever (short throw) 2, joystick 2. Fine adjustment: round knob (large diameter) 1; cont. thumbwheel 2, crank (many turns) 2, lever (long throw) 3, joystick 2. Single-coordinate tracking: lever 1, crank 2, knob 3. Two-coordinate tracking: joystick/ball/mouse 1, crank 3.
site_hook: Lookup table keyed by function x control type; show rank when user tags a control object

title: Recommended manual controls by actuation force
text: Small actuation force: 2 discrete positions - key lock, legend switch, push button, slide switch, toggle switch; 3 discrete - push button, rotary selector, toggle; 4 to 24 discrete - rotary selector switch; continuous setting (linear and less than 360°) - continuous rotary knob, joystick or lever; continuous slewing and fine adjustment - continuous rotary knob, crank, joystick or lever. Large actuation force: 2 discrete - detent lever, foot push button, hand push button; 3 to 24 discrete - detent lever, rotary selector switch; continuous setting (linear and less than 360°) - crank, handwheel, joystick or lever, two-axis grip handle; continuous setting (greater than 360°) - crank, handwheel, two-axis grip handle, valve.
site_hook: Lookup table keyed by function and force class

title: Combined controls compatibility
text: When several controls are combined in one device, responses shall be compatible with control movement (e.g., right motion = clockwise roll, right turn, movement right).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: User-control orientation
text: Controls shall be oriented with respect to the user. Where a vehicle user may use two or more stations, controls shall cause movement oriented to the user at the effecting station unless remote visual reference is used.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Valve control direction
text: Rotary valve controls shall open the valve with a counterclockwise motion.
site_hook: Checklist item / attribute of handwheel object

title: Labeling of valve controls
text: Valve controls shall be provided with double-ended arrows showing direction of operation and labeled at each end (e.g., open and close).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Ball valve controls
text: Ball valves with lever handles shall have valve position indication (open/closed) and double-ended arrows showing direction of operation.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Grouping of controls with displays
text: Controls operated in a task-driven sequence or together shall be grouped together along with their associated displays. Steps selected by one control shall be arranged by order of occurrence (5.1.1.3.1.1); unnecessary cycling through ON/OFF shall be avoided (5.1.1.3.1.2).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Sequential operation arrangement
text: Where sequential operations follow a fixed pattern, controls shall be arranged to facilitate operation (e.g., left-to-right/top-to-bottom).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Location of primary controls
text: The most important and frequently used controls (particularly rotary controls and those requiring fine settings) shall have the most favorable position for ease of reaching and grasping.
site_hook: User tags controls as primary; site checks they lie within the comfortable (not just maximum) reach zone of the P5 mannequin and near the hand's neutral position

title: Consistency of arrangement
text: Arrangement of functionally similar or identical primary controls shall be consistent from panel to panel and across systems.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Remote controls
text: Controls operated remote from the display/equipment/vehicle shall be arranged to facilitate direction-of-movement consistency.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Maintenance and adjustment controls
text: Controls used solely for maintenance and adjustment shall be covered during normal operation but readily accessible and visible when required.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Spacing between controls
text: Minimum spacing between controls shall comply with table III; spacing between a control and an adjacent obstruction per the figures referenced in table III. Minimum spacing shall be increased for gloves, mittens, or CBRNE or other mission-required PPE when such operation is a system requirement.
site_hook: Sandbox control objects with type; compute edge-to-edge distance between pairs and compare with Table III / per-type figure; apply glove increase

title: Minimum edge-to-edge separation between different mechanical control types
limits: edge-to-edge separation: >= 13 mm [toggle switch to push button (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 19 mm [toggle switch to continuous rotary control (0.75 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 19 mm [toggle switch to rotary selector switch (0.75 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 13 mm [toggle switch to discrete thumbwheel (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 13 mm [push button to continuous rotary control (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 13 mm [push button to rotary selector switch (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 13 mm [push button to discrete thumbwheel (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 25 mm [continuous rotary control to rotary selector switch (1 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 19 mm [continuous rotary control to discrete thumbwheel (0.75 in); one hand, bare hand] | edge-to-edge separation: >= 19 mm [rotary selector switch to discrete thumbwheel (0.75 in); one hand, bare hand]
text: Minimum edge-to-edge separation (one-hand, bare-handed operation; push buttons not separated by barriers): toggle-push button 13 mm (0.5 in); toggle-continuous rotary 19 mm (0.75 in); toggle-rotary selector 19 mm (0.75 in); toggle-discrete thumbwheel 13 mm (0.5 in); push button-continuous rotary 13 mm (0.5 in); push button-rotary selector 13 mm (0.5 in); push button-discrete thumbwheel 13 mm (0.5 in); continuous rotary-rotary selector 25 mm (1 in); continuous rotary-discrete thumbwheel 19 mm (0.75 in); rotary selector-discrete thumbwheel 19 mm (0.75 in). Same-type pairs: toggle see figure 16; push buttons see figure 14; continuous rotary see figure 12 (as printed); rotary selector see figure 6; discrete thumbwheel see figure 8.
site_hook: Pairwise edge distance between typed control objects on a panel; flag pairs below matrix value

title: Control interference
text: Size, shape, and location of controls shall ensure that operating any one control does not interfere with the use of other controls or other duties.
site_hook: Check hand/arm volume of mannequin while operating one control does not collide with other control objects

title: Emergency shutoff controls
text: Emergency shutoff controls shall be accessible, not hidden, located to prevent accidental activation, and positioned within easy reach of the user.
site_hook: Tag control as emergency; verify within reach envelope of P5 mannequin in operating posture (restrained if applicable)
percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

title: Advantages/disadvantages of control coding modes
text: Table IV compares location, shape, size, mode of operation, labeling and color coding (visual/nonvisual identification, low illumination, glove use, extra space, etc.).
site_hook: Reference only

title: Consistent application of coding
text: Where coding differentiates controls, application of the code shall be uniform throughout the system and other systems the user operates.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Location coding: controls beside or behind user
limits: separation between location-coded controls beside/behind user: >= 250 mm [10 in]
text: When controls are beside or behind the user, they shall be a minimum of 250 mm (10 in) apart for location coding.
site_hook: Compute distance between control objects located lateral/behind the mannequin's frontal plane; flag if < 250 mm

title: Location coding: similar functions
text: Controls associated with similar functions shall be in the same relative location from workstation to workstation and panel to panel.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Size coding: number of sizes
limits: number of size codes: <= 3 count [absolute size discrimination]
text: No more than three different sizes shall be used to code controls for discrimination by absolute size.
site_hook: Count distinct sizes among size-coded control objects

title: Size coding: same function same size
text: Controls used for the same function on different items of equipment shall be the same size.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Size coding: knob diameter difference
limits: knob diameter difference: >= 13 mm [0.5 in]
text: When knob diameter is the coding parameter, differences between diameters shall be not less than 13 mm (0.5 in).
site_hook: Compare diameters of size-coded knob objects

title: Size coding: knob thickness difference
limits: knob thickness difference: >= 10 mm [0.4 in]
text: When knob thickness is the coding parameter, differences between thicknesses shall be not less than 10 mm (0.4 in).
site_hook: Compare thicknesses of size-coded knob objects

title: Shape coding criteria
text: Shape coding may be used for identification by feel. When used: coded feature shall not interfere with manipulation; shapes identifiable by hand and eye regardless of position/orientation; tactually identifiable with gloves; positively and non-reversibly attached to shafts (5.1.1.4.4.1.5); easily recognizable shapes for touch-alone knobs (figure 1) (5.1.1.4.4.1.6); clearly associated with intended function (5.1.1.4.4.1.7).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Number of shapes
limits: number of shape codes: <= 10 count [absolute discrimination]
text: Number of shapes to be identified by each user by absolute discrimination shall be not more than 10.
site_hook: Count distinct shape codes

title: Minimum dimensions for shape-coded controls
limits: height: >= 13 mm [0.5 in] | width: >= 13 mm [0.5 in] | depth: >= 6.5 mm [0.25 in]
text: Minimum control dimensions when users must distinguish controls by shape alone: a. Height 13 mm (0.5 in) or larger; b. Width 13 mm (0.5 in) or larger; c. Depth 6.5 mm (0.25 in) or larger.
site_hook: Control knob object dimensions vs minima when shape-coded

title: Color coding limits
limits: number of coding colors: <= 5 count
text: Colors shall not be the sole means of control coding. Not more than five colors shall be used (5.1.1.4.5.1). Controls shall be black (SAE AMS-STD-595 17038, 27038, 37038) or gray (26231 or 36231) (5.1.1.4.5.2). Coding colors limited to red 11105/21105, green 14187, orange-yellow 13538/23538/33538, white 17875/27875/37875, blue 15123 if absolutely necessary (5.1.1.4.5.3). No gloss finishes where glare/friction degrades performance or in darkened areas (5.1.1.4.5.4-5).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Blind operation separation
limits: separation for blind-operated controls (if not shape coded): >= 125 mm [5 in]
text: Where 'blind' operation is necessary, hand controls shall be shape coded, or separated from adjacent controls by at least 125 mm (5 in).
site_hook: User flags control as blind-operated; compute distance to nearest control object

title: Prevention of accidental actuation: location and design
text: Controls shall be designed and located so they are not susceptible to being moved accidentally, particularly critical controls. Internal/hidden controls protected (5.1.1.7.2); protection shall not preclude operation within required time (5.1.1.7.3).
site_hook: Check that critical control objects are not inside swept volumes of mannequin during ingress/egress or other control operation

title: Methods of protection against accidental actuation
text: One or more of: a. locate/orient so user unlikely to strike it; b. recess/shield/barriers (control entirely contained within recess or barrier envelope); c. cover or guard (no safety or lock wire); d. interlock; e. movement resistance; f. lock against passing through positions; g. rotary action; h. spring-loaded depress-to-turn.
site_hook: Checklist item; (b) could be geometric check that control does not protrude beyond barrier envelope

title: Weapon fire trigger protection
text: Weapon (or directed energy) fire trigger/switch shall be clearly labeled and physically protected; trigger shall be guarded positive-action requiring continuous intent (5.1.1.7.6). Dead man controls shall be used wherever user incapacity can produce a critical condition (5.1.1.7.7).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Feedback / time lag
text: No discernible time lag between system condition change and its display; unavoidable lag requires immediate feedback; feedback shall indicate actuation and response.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Hazardous operations
text: Critical position of a control initiating hazardous operations shall activate visible and audible warnings in the affected area; critical/emergency control dedicated to that function only.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Control location relative to display
text: A control shall be located adjacent to (normally below or to the right of) its associated display and positioned so that neither the control nor the hand normally used for setting the control will obscure the display.
site_hook: Link control to display objects; check control is below/right of display and that mannequin hand/arm at the control does not intersect the eye-to-display sight line

title: Control/display relationship apparent
text: Relationship of control to display shall be immediately apparent and unambiguous, through proximity, grouping, coding, framing, labeling (5.1.2.1.3); complexity/precision consistent with system and user ability (5.1.2.1.4-5).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: System response times (Table V)
limits: key response: <= 0.1 s | key print: <= 0.2 s | page turn: <= 1.0 s | page scan: <= 0.5 s | XY entry: <= 0.2 s | pointing: <= 0.2 s | sketching: <= 0.2 s | local update: <= 0.5 s | host update: <= 2.0 s | file update: <= 10 s | inquiry simple: <= 2.0 s | inquiry complex: <= 10 s | error feedback: <= 0.2 s
text: Maximum system response times for real-time systems shall not exceed Table V: key response 0.1 s; key print 0.2 s; page turn 1.0 s; page scan 0.5 s; XY entry 0.2 s; pointing 0.2 s; sketching 0.2 s; local update 0.5 s; host update 2.0 s; file update 10 s; inquiry (simple) 2.0 s; inquiry (complex) 10 s; error feedback 0.2 s.
site_hook: Not geometric; could be a manual checklist

title: Information-system feedback and error management (summary)
limits: delay requiring processing message: >= 1 s | delay requiring countdown: >= 10 s
text: 5.1.2.1.6.1-5.1.2.1.7.13: feedback on status, input confirmation, processing messages when response > 1 s, countdown when delay > 10 s, startup feedback, rejection reasons, error correction and checking, critical entry acknowledgement, etc. Software dialog items, summarized only.
site_hook: Out of scope for geometry; manual checklist at most

title: Control illumination adjustability
limits: dimming increments: >= 30 count | minimum dim level: <= 0.02 % of full bright
text: Adjustable illumination shall be provided for controls (including labels/markings) read in darkened conditions; continuously adjustable or at least 30 increments from full bright to full off; continuous intensity control from full bright to 0.02 percent of full bright and off.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Simultaneous access by multiple crew
text: If more than one crewmember must have simultaneous access to a group of controls or displays, each user shall have physical and visual access to all controls, displays and communication needed for assigned tasks.
site_hook: Place several mannequins at their stations; check each assigned control is within that mannequin's reach and each display within its line of sight/visual field

title: Functional grouping and sequence
text: Functionally related controls and displays shall be located close together in functional groups; groups ordered left-to-right (preferred) or top-to-bottom (5.1.2.2.1.1); more frequently used and most important groups in areas of easiest access (5.1.2.2.1.3).
site_hook: User tags groups and frequency; check frequent groups are in preferred reach/visual zone

title: Functional group outline: non-critical
limits: border width: 1.5-1.5 mm [0.0625 in; non-critical group]
text: Where functional group coding is specified and gray panels are used, non-critical functional groups shall be outlined with a black border measuring 1.5 mm (0.0625 in) (SAE AMS-STD-595/27038).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Functional group outline: critical
limits: border width: 5-5 mm [0.1875 in as printed; critical/emergency group]
text: Panels involving emergency or extremely critical operations shall be outlined with a red border measuring 5 mm (0.1875 in) (SAE AMS-STD-595/21136) or designated by contrasting color pads; orange-yellow and black striped border under red lighting (5.1.2.2.1.4.4).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Consistency and no mirror images
text: Location of recurring functional groups and items shall be consistent panel to panel; mirror image arrangements shall not be used (5.1.2.2.1.5.1).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Maintenance control/display groups
text: Groups solely for maintenance shall be in positions of lesser access relative to operating groups.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Arrangement within groups
text: Within groups, controls/displays located by operational sequence or function; otherwise by importance or frequency with the most important/frequent in the most accessible locations. Horizontal display rows associated with horizontal controls; vertical columns with vertical controls (5.1.2.2.3.2, 5.1.2.2.3.4); if fewer control rows, top-row display controls at left (5.1.2.2.3.3).
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Simultaneous use: viewing angle
text: A visual display that must be monitored while a related control is manipulated shall be located so the user is not required to observe the display from an extreme visual angle (to maintain legibility and avoid parallax).
site_hook: With the mannequin's hand on the control, measure angle between eye-to-display line and display normal; flag large angles (see 5.2 limits; figure 2 shows instrument face at minimum 45° to normal line of sight)

title: Control for multiple displays
text: If one control requires reading several displays, the control shall be as near as possible to them and preferably beneath the middle of the displays, not obscuring them. Rotary selector sequence corresponds to displays; OFF position most counterclockwise; unselected displays read off-scale (5.1.2.2.3.6.1-3).
site_hook: Compute horizontal offset of control from centroid of linked displays; occlusion check

title: Combined (ganged) control placement
text: Displays affected by a combined control shall be arranged left to right with the combined control underneath the center of the displays, not obscuring them.

title: Display remains visible
text: Controls shall be located so the user's hand or arm does not obscure the associated display.
site_hook: Ray-cast from mannequin eye to linked display while hand is at control; flag occlusion by hand/forearm

title: Separated control and display panels
text: When controls are on panels separate from their displays, the panels shall be adjacent and mounted at approximately the same direction relative to the user; preferred display panel above control panel; not mounted facing each other; control positions correspond to display positions.
site_hook: Compare panel normals/orientation; check display panel above control panel

Metallic labels mounted to prevent galvanic corrosion (5.4.8.4).

title: Labels on flat surfaces; curved labels
text: Whenever practicable, labels should be mounted on a flat surface; curved labels (wrapped around pipe or cable) should be avoided (5.4.8.7). If on a curved surface, lettering shall be completely visible from the normal viewing position (5.4.8.8). When curvature makes lettering too small to read, another mode of labeling such as an attached tag shall be used (5.4.8.10).

text: The crew compartment heating system shall be capable of maintaining temperatures above 20 °C (68 °F) during occupancy when personnel are not wearing arctic clothing and exposure exceeds 3 hours; achieved within 1 hour after heater turned on (5.6.6.1.2).

title: Air temperature uniformity around body

title: Hot surface contact limits (Table XXVII)
limits: surface temp, momentary contact, metal: <= 60 °C | surface temp, momentary contact, glass: <= 68 °C | surface temp, momentary contact, plastic or wood: <= 85 °C | surface temp, prolonged contact, metal: <= 49 °C | surface temp, prolonged contact, glass: <= 59 °C | surface temp, prolonged contact, plastic or wood: <= 69 °C
text: Heaters shall be located or protected so personnel cannot touch parts hot enough to cause burns. Table XXVII: momentary contact metal 60 °C (140 °F), glass 68 °C (154 °F), plastic or wood 85 °C (185 °F); prolonged contact or handling metal 49 °C (120 °F), glass 59 °C (138 °F), plastic or wood 69 °C (156 °F).
site_hook: Object material + temperature parameter; flag if within mannequin reach/contact and above limit

title: Air velocity at head location

title: Air conditioning trigger

site_hook: Not geometric

title: Night display luminance range

title: Egress path lighting manual activation

title: Squad ingress time

title: Two egress paths per position

title: Non-skid step surfaces

site_hook: Checklist

title: Crew and squad emergency egress time
limits: emergency egress time: <= 30 s
text: The maximum time for the crew and squad to egress the vehicle in an emergency from primary or secondary egress points shall be not more than 30 seconds.
site_hook: Trial/checklist

title: No tools to egress
text: Vehicle occupants shall not require tools or special equipment to leave their seated position or to open egress points.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Trip hazards
text: Vehicle components or subsystems shall not present a tripping hazard to occupants ingressing or egressing the vehicle.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Rescue of incapacitated person
text: The ground vehicle design shall accommodate the rescue of a wounded or incapacitated person from the vehicle's interior; first responders shall be able to access the interior via at least one entry point regardless of vehicle orientation (5.6.8.2.2).

title: Rescue tunnel dimensions

title: Vehicle step heights and spacing

text: If ingress/egress, equipment access, service access, or exterior step locations are greater than 450 mm (18 in) above ground, the vehicle shall have handholds and footholds such that the first step is between 375 and 450 mm (15 and 18 in) above the ground and all subsequent steps are approximately equally spaced between 225 and 375 mm (9 and 15 in) apart, with 300 mm (12 in) preferred.

text: It shall be obvious when a cover is not in place or is not securely fastened; non-obvious opening methods shall have permanent instructions on the outside (5.9.10.3) using simple symbols or words like 'push' (5.9.10.3.1).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Ventilation hole size
limits: ventilation hole diameter: <= 13 mm [in covers/shields]
text: If a cover or shield requires ventilation holes, the holes shall be not larger than 13 mm (0.5 in) in diameter.
site_hook: Cover object vent-hole diameter parameter; compare also with mannequin finger breadth (finger-probe concept)

title: Hazards spaced back from ventilation holes
text: Any component that rotates, oscillates, or carries high voltage shall be spaced back from ventilation holes so personnel cannot accidentally contact the hazard.
site_hook: Finger length (mannequin hand) vs set-back distance behind vent holes; no number given

title: Grasp areas on access covers
text: Access covers shall be equipped with grasp areas or other means for opening them; non-removable covers should be retainable open (5.9.10.8.1).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Covers accommodate handwear
text: Covers shall accommodate handwear or other special clothing that may be worn by maintenance personnel.
site_hook: Grasp-area/finger recess sizes vs gloved hand dimensions (use Figure 57 gloved values)

title: Adjacent hinged doors open opposite
text: When hinged doors are adjacent, they shall open in opposite directions to maximize accessibility.
site_hook: Door objects hinge-side parameter

title: Sweep volume for hinged covers
text: If covers are hinged, space equal to the sweep volume of the cover should be allowed so the body frame and brackets will not obstruct its opening.
site_hook: Door/hatch swing arc collision check with other sandbox objects

title: Door stops/retainers
text: Stops or retainers shall be used as necessary to keep doors from swinging into adjacent controls or fragile components and so they will not spring their hinges.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Rounded edges on doors and covers
text: Sharp edges and corners on doors, covers, and other exposed surfaces that might present a safety hazard shall be rounded in accordance with 5.7.6.4.
site_hook: Object edge-radius parameter vs 5.7.6.4

title: Minimize fastener number and diversity
text: Number and diversity of fasteners shall be minimized; locations of differing fasteners distinguishable (5.9.11.1.1); identical fasteners not used where wrong removal causes damage (5.9.11.1.2); finger/hand-operated fasteners preferred (5.9.11.1.3); fasteners shall not require non-standard tools (5.9.11.1.4).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Captive fasteners
text: Captive fasteners shall be used where dropping or losing them could cause damage or hazardous removal problems, and for access covers requiring frequent removal (5.9.11.4).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Latches and catches
text: Latches and catches shall give clear visual indication of engagement; spring/snap-down force shall not be so strong it could injure personnel (5.9.11.5.1); located to avoid inadvertent operation (5.9.11.5.2).
site_hook: Checklist

title: High-torque fasteners external hex; direct tool access
limits: fastener torque threshold for external hex: >= 14 N*m [more than 14 N*m (10 ft*lbf)]
text: External hex or external double-hex wrenching elements should be provided on all fasteners requiring more than 14 newton-meters (10 foot-pounds-force) of torque; direct tool access shall be provided to allow torquing without swivel or universal joint extensions.
site_hook: User-entered fastener torque; direct straight tool path check (tool clearance)

title: Low-torque fastener head types
limits: fastener torque: <= 14 N*m [less than 14 N*m (10 ft*lbf)]
text: External hex, internal hex, combination head, or star fasteners shall be provided where less than 14 newton-meters (10 foot-pounds-force) torque is required; straight-slot or cross-recess internal grip fasteners should not be used except wood fasteners or standard commercial items.
site_hook: User-entered fastener type/torque

title: One-hand/one-tool nuts and bolts
text: Nuts and bolts removed frequently and relatively inaccessible shall be removable/replaceable with one hand or one tool; nut or bolt semi-permanently attached (5.9.11.6.12).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Hand or tool clearance at nuts and bolts
text: Nuts and bolts shall have hand or tool clearance for easy operation.
site_hook: Use Figure 56 tool envelopes (e.g. open-end wrench 270 x 200 mm, 60 deg swing) around fastener

title: Lubrication points accessible
text: Lubrication and reservoir checking shall be possible without disassembly (5.9.12.2); lubrication points shall be accessible, clearly labeled, with captive caps where applicable (5.9.12.5); extended fittings for ports not readily accessible or visible (5.9.12.6).
site_hook: Reach + line-of-sight check to lube-point markers

title: Cable coding interval
limits: cable code interval: <= 300 mm [common-sheath cables]
text: Cables containing individually insulated conductors with a common sheath shall be coded every 300 mm (12 in).
site_hook: Not a body-dimension check; checklist

title: Cable clamp spacing
limits: clamp spacing: <= 610 mm [or as specified (6.2)]
text: Clamps or plates that mount lines and cables shall have heat-insulating liners and be spaced not more than 610 mm (24 in) apart or as specified.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Cables not used as handholds or steps
text: Interconnecting cables shall be routed to minimize use as handholds or steps; a protective guard shall be placed over lines/cables where such use is possible (5.9.13.4.2); routing shall not obstruct visual or physical access (5.9.13.4).
site_hook: Flag cable objects within mannequin hand/foot reach along climbing paths (ladder/step postures)

title: Lines and cables accessible
text: Lines and cables shall be accessible without disassembling other equipment (5.9.13.5.1), with accesses and clearances for removal/replacement (5.9.13.5.3), and routed to be accessible for inspection (5.9.13.7).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Wire number code interval
limits: wire number code repeat interval: <= 500 mm
text: Number codes shall be repeated every 500 mm (20 in) over the entire length of the wire.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Fluid connectors - no jacking
text: Connectors for pipes, tubing, and hoses shall be located so that it is unnecessary to jack the equipment up to drain, fill, or perform other maintenance.
site_hook: Reach check from standing/kneeling mannequin to drain/fill point without supine posture

title: Quick-disconnect plugs (one turn)
limits: turns to secure connector: <= 1 turns [not more than one complete turn]
text: Plugs requiring not more than one turn or other quick-disconnect plugs shall be provided whenever feasible; connectors shall plug in or secure with not more than one complete turn (5.9.14.13.2).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Connector labels visible
text: Labels or codes on connectors shall be visible during maintenance whether connected or disconnected; connectors identifiable without disconnecting (5.9.14.4.2).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Connector spacing for grasp
text: Connectors shall be spaced far enough apart that they can be grasped firmly; spacing between adjacent connectors or a connector and an obstruction shall be compatible with plug size/shape and clothing worn (cold weather handwear, CBRNE gloves, PPE) (5.9.14.7.1).
site_hook: Connector marker objects with spacing; handwear selector

title: Connector spacing - bare fingers
limits: spacing between adjacent connectors: >= 25 mm [bare finger operation] | swept clearance arc (sequential removal exception): >= 270 deg [with 25 mm clearance]
text: For bare finger operation, spacing between adjacent connectors shall be not less than 25 mm (1 in), except where connectors are sequentially removed and replaced and 25 mm (1 in) clearance is provided in a swept area of not less than 270 degrees around each connector at the start of its removal and replacement sequence.
site_hook: Connector objects; edge-to-edge gap measured from outermost portion (5.9.14.7.4)

title: Connector spacing - gloved/grip/mittened
limits: spacing between adjacent connectors: >= 32 mm [gloved fingers] | spacing between adjacent connectors: >= 64 mm [connector must be gripped firmly] | spacing between adjacent connectors: >= 75 mm [mittened hands] | swept clearance arc (sequential removal exception): >= 270 deg [with full specified clearance]
text: Spacing between adjacent connectors shall be not less than 32 mm (1.25 in) if operated with gloved fingers, 64 mm (2.5 in) if the connector must be gripped firmly, and 75 mm (3 in) if operated with mittened hands; may be reduced where connectors are sequentially removed and full clearance is provided in a swept area of not less than 270 degrees around each connector.
site_hook: Connector objects + handwear selector

title: Connector spacing measurement
text: Spacing shall be measured from the outermost portion of the connector (backshell, strain relief clamp, dust cover, or EMI/RFI shield).
site_hook: Defines measurement method for 5.9.14.7.2-3

title: Space for connector wrench
text: Where high torque is required to tighten or loosen the connector, space shall be provided for use of a connector wrench.
site_hook: Tool clearance envelope around connector

title: Rear of plug connectors accessible
text: The rear of plug connectors shall be accessible for testing and servicing, except where precluded by potting, sealing, or other requirements.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Fuses readily accessible
text: Fuses shall be readily accessible for removal and replacement; no other components shall require removal to access fuses (5.9.16.2.2.1); no special tools unless required by safety (5.9.16.2.2.2).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Circuit breakers within reach in operating posture
text: When resetting of circuit breakers is permissible and required for system operation during a mission, the breakers shall be located within reach of maintenance personnel in their normal operating posture.
site_hook: Reach-to-target from mannequin in operating posture (e.g. seated/vehicle) to breaker panel target; P5 female reach governs
percentile_rule: smallest user (e.g. P5 female) functional reach

title: Circuit breaker dimensions and separation
text: Dimensions and separation for toggle bat actuated circuit breakers shall be in accordance with figure 16; for legend switch actuated circuit breakers in accordance with figure 17.
site_hook: Cross-reference to toggle switch / legend switch checks of 5.1

title: Test and service point design/location criteria
text: Test and service points should be located by frequency of use; distinguishable; with positive indication of adjustment; at central panel(s); with leads/extended fittings to bring hard-to-reach points to an accessible area; not isolated; not concealed by braces, brackets or structure.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Test points close to adjustment controls/displays
text: Test points used for adjustment shall be located sufficiently close to the controls and displays used in the adjustment so that place-to-place movement is not required; they shall be physically and visually accessible in the installed condition without removing other items (5.9.17.2.2).
site_hook: From one mannequin position: hand reach to test point and control, and eye line-of-sight to display, all satisfied simultaneously

title: Test points face maintainer
text: Test points and their labels and controls shall face the maintenance personnel; located on surfaces or behind accesses easily reached when fully assembled and installed (5.9.17.5).
site_hook: Target surface normal vs eye direction; reach check

title: Test point minimum clearance
limits: clearance around test point: >= 19 mm [finger control only] | clearance around test point: >= 75 mm [gloved hand]
text: Test points shall be located so that a minimum clearance of 19 mm (0.75 in) is provided when only finger control is required and 75 mm (3.0 in) is provided when a gloved hand must be used.
site_hook: Test-point marker clearance to nearest object; handwear selector

title: Test point guards and shields
text: Test points shall have guards and shields to protect personnel and equipment, particularly if serviced while operating; isolated positions avoided (5.9.17.8); windows for frequent visual inspection (5.9.17.9); tool guides for blind operation (5.9.17.10).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Test points within functional reach of related controls
text: Test points shall be located within easy functional reach or seeing distance of related or corresponding controls, displays, fittings, and switches.
site_hook: Distance test point <-> related control within mannequin functional reach envelope; eye-to-display distance

title: Test points away from hazards
limits: distance from test point to hazard: >= 115 mm [electrical, mechanical, or other hazards]
text: Test points shall be located at least 115 mm (4.5 in) away from electrical, mechanical, or other hazards.
site_hook: Point-to-point distance test-point marker to hazard marker

title: Test equipment instructions readable during operation
text: Instructions for operating portable test equipment shall be directly readable while the equipment is operated; printed large enough to be seen in the lowest light level likely (5.9.18.2.2).
site_hook: Eye-to-label viewing distance check; letter size vs distance per 5.4

title: Harness or sling for portable test equipment
text: An adjustable harness or sling should be provided to facilitate carrying portable or handheld test equipment.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Stands or casters threshold
limits: device mass requiring stands or casters: >= 13.6 kg [more than 13.6 kg (30 lb)]
text: Stands or casters shall be provided for devices weighing more than 13.6 kg (30 lb).
site_hook: Box/tool object mass > 13.6 kg -> require stands or casters

title: Wheels, casters or hoist threshold
limits: device mass requiring wheels/casters/hoist: >= 40.8 kg [more than 40.8 kg (90 lb)]
text: Wheels, casters, or hoist-lifting shall be provided for devices weighing more than 40.8 kg (90 lb).
site_hook: Box/tool object mass > 40.8 kg -> require wheels, casters or hoist

title: Rounded corners on portable test equipment
text: Portable test equipment shall have rounded corners and edges in accordance with 5.7.6.4.
site_hook: Edge radius parameter vs 5.7.6.4

title: Portable test equipment carry weight
text: The weight of test equipment for portability shall be in accordance with the carrying weight limits of 5.20.4.
site_hook: Carrying posture + box/tool mass vs 5.20.4 limits

title: Handheld test equipment weight
limits: handheld test equipment mass: <= 2.3 (preferred 1.4) kg [shall not exceed 2.3 kg; preferably not exceed 1.4 kg]
text: The weight of handheld test equipment shall not exceed 2.3 kg (5 lb), and preferably not exceed 1.4 kg (3 lb).
site_hook: Sandbox tool object mass: fail > 2.3 kg, warn > 1.4 kg

title: Serrated/ridged underside of handheld test equipment
text: The underside of handheld test equipment should be serrated or ridged to prevent slipping out of the maintainer's hand.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Minimize number of tools; common tools
text: Equipment shall minimize numbers, types, and complexity of tools (5.9.19.1); only tools in normal tool kit should be required (5.9.19.3); special tools only when common tools cannot be used or give significant advantage (5.9.19.4).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Tool full range of motion
text: The design shall provide for effective use of tools through their full range of motion.
site_hook: Tool swing envelope collision check; tie to Figure 56 openings

title: Tool grip span
text: The grip span for tools should be appropriate for the anticipated tasks to minimize effort and maximize torque.
site_hook: Tool object grip span vs mannequin hand grip-breadth / hand length percentile

title: Tool wrist thongs
text: Tools used where dropping could cause delay or loss should be provided with thongs long enough to place a loop over the wrist.
site_hook: Could use mannequin wrist circumference/hand breadth for loop size

title: Heat/cold-resistant tool handles
text: Heat- or cold-resistant handles should be used on tools used in extreme climates; metal handles undesirable in cold and hot climates; serrated gripping surfaces (5.9.19.11.1).
site_hook: Checklist

title: PCB finger access and gripping aids
text: Printed circuit boards shall be designed and mounted for ease of removal and replacement, considering finger access, gripping aids, and resistance created by the mounting device.
site_hook: Checklist; finger access sizes from Figure 57

title: Stored energy release
text: Devices operating under stored energy shall be designed so energy can be safely released or constrained before maintenance; means immediately apparent (5.9.21.2); cannot be inadvertently reactivated (5.9.21.3); labeled with DANGER hazard warning (5.9.21.4).
site_hook: Checklist

title: Battery removal by one person
text: One person should be capable of removing batteries for servicing and replacing them without removing other equipment and without special tools; battery holders tool-free (5.9.21.5.2).
site_hook: Battery as box object: mass vs one-person limits (5.9.3.11.1, 5.20) and reach/lift posture

title: Hydraulic line identification interval
limits: hydraulic line identification interval: <= 450 mm [and at both ends]
text: Inlets, outlets, and connecting lines in hydraulic systems shall be identified at least every 450 mm (18 in) and at both ends.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Drain cock handle down = closed
text: All drain cocks shall be closed when the handle is in the down position.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Hydraulic connectors standard tools
text: Connectors in hydraulic systems shall be of standard design and manipulated with standard tools.
site_hook: Checklist

title: Population accommodation for workspace design
limits: multivariate accommodation (each sex): >= 90 (preferred 95) % of population | univariate accommodation (each sex): >= 95 % of population [should; central 95% = P2.5 to P97.5]
text: Unless otherwise specified, design of DoD systems, equipment and facilities shall accommodate the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped females of the target user population (see 5.8), using dimensions applicable to the task. For univariate accommodation, the central 95 percent of the male and the central 95 percent of the female target user population should be used.

text: The design shall consider both the appropriate workspace and the workstation assets for personnel to achieve a defined task (see 5.10.3.5).

limits: vertical offset monitor top vs eye height: (preferred 0) cm [top of screen at eye level] | lateral offset monitor centre vs keyboard centre: (preferred 0) cm [monitor directly in line with keyboard]

title: Personnel considerations
text: In establishing the workspace, consideration shall be given to user body postures required, whether the work is fixed, mobile or temporary, the environment, and the number of personnel required.

title: Postures considered
text: Workspace design shall consider the body postures to include standing, sitting, squatting, and kneeling, among other relevant postures.

title: Neutral posture
text: To the maximum extent possible, a workspace shall allow personnel to maintain a neutral posture.

title: Changing posture
text: To the maximum extent possible, a workspace shall be designed to allow personnel to change their posture (e.g. between standing and sitting) while maintaining the ability to remain neutral.

title: Forward reach: lifting and torque in neutral posture

limits: kick space depth: >= 10 cm [[4 in]] | kick space height: >= 10 cm [[4 in]]
text: All cabinets, workstations, consoles, and work surfaces shall contain a kick space at the base at least 10 cm (4 in) deep and 10 cm (4 in) high to allow for standard footwear. Some oversized boots, such as the Arctic cold-weather boot, may require a larger kick space.

Boot length 40 cm (16 in); b. Boot height 29.2 cm (11.5 in); c. Toe height 11.4 cm (4.5 in); d. Boot width 15.2 cm (6 in).

title: Physical environment design
text: Physical environment and associated equipment design shall systematically incorporate the influence of tasks, performance capabilities, physical dimensions, and viewing angles for operator and maintainer personnel.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Traffic areas
text: Traffic area and flow design should consider task activities around workstations, minimal interference between workstations and traffic, equipment movements, normal/worst/emergency traffic, and collision avoidance.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Layout to minimize congestion
text: Equipment and workstations shall be located to minimize congestion in workflow or personnel movement and to minimize interference with personnel traffic areas.
site_hook: Check workstation free-floor zones do not overlap traffic lanes

title: Group equipment by maintainer
text: Equipment maintained by the same person should be grouped together.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Visual inspection points easily seen
text: Components that require frequent visual inspection of check points, adjustment points, cable-end connections, and labels should be located in positions that can be seen easily.
site_hook: Line of sight from maintainer eye point to tagged inspection points

title: Equipment arrangement for multiple workers
text: When two or more people share a workspace, equipment shall be arranged for sharing, minimal communications needs, face-to-face communication, and minimal mutual interference.
site_hook: Multiple mannequins: reach-envelope overlap and mutual line of sight

title: Layout for safety, criticality and frequency
text: All equipment shall be located to minimize equipment damage, personnel injury, or inadvertent actuation; the most critical units shall be the most accessible; where criticality is not a factor, units with more total use shall be more accessible.
site_hook: Rank tagged units by criticality/frequency vs reach distance from operator

title: Floor space for work and passage
text: Floor space shall ensure: work and aisle spaces do not overlap; handling tasks including turning space size the spaces; spaces kept clean and in repair; storage does not interfere; free of protrusions, holes, loose materials; permanent aisles marked; covers and guardrails over pits, tanks, vats and ditches; floor loading limits displayed; sufficient space around electrical equipment.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Free floor space in front of racks and cabinets
limits: free floor depth in front of rack/cabinet: >= 1.2 m [[48 in]]
text: Free floor space of at least 1.2 m (48 in) is provided in front of each equipment rack and cabinet.
site_hook: Sandbox rack/cabinet (box) object: clear floor depth in front

title: Spacing between rows of cabinets with drawers
limits: aisle between cabinet rows minus deepest drawer depth: >= 200 mm [[8 in]]
text: The minimum space between rows of cabinets containing drawers shall be 200 mm (8 in) greater than the depth of the deepest drawer.
site_hook: Needs drawer depth parameter on cabinet object; aisle width check

title: Lateral workspace at racks with drawers/removable equipment
limits: lateral clearance, one side (item < 20 kg): >= 460 mm [[18 in]] | lateral clearance, other side (item < 20 kg): >= 100 mm [[4 in]] | lateral clearance, each side (item > 20 kg): >= 460 mm [[18 in]; two-person access] | item mass threshold: <= 20 kg [[44 lb]]
text: Measured from drawers or equipment in the extended position: a. items weighing less than 20 kg (44 lb): 460 mm (18 in) on one side and 100 mm (4 in) on the other; b. items weighing more than 20 kg (44 lb): 460 mm (18 in) on each side (two-person access).
site_hook: Box object with mass: lateral clearance either side of extended drawer/unit

title: Rear access space
text: When a maintainer is to access the back of an entire rack or panel-mounted unit, it shall be installed with sufficient clearance to perform all required maintenance, including removal of rear panels.
site_hook: Clearance behind rack vs maintainer mannequin posture envelope (Figure 59/60)
percentile_rule: Fit P95 male

title: Maintenance separation
text: Maintenance workplaces, controls and displays should be separate from operational ones; maintainer-only controls/displays should not be visible to operators but readily accessible to maintainers.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Protection and guarding at accesses
text: Protection shall be provided against potential hazards while performing tasks. If a hazardous condition (e.g. exposed high-voltage conductors) exists behind an access, the barrier shall have an interlock that de-energizes the equipment when open, and the hazard and interlock shall be noted on the case/cover visibly when the access is open.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Non-skid top surfaces used as platforms
text: Top surfaces of equipment shall be reinforced and provided with non-skid surfaces whenever used as work platforms.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Features to assist personnel
text: Auxiliary hooks, holders, lights, outlets, non-skid treads, expanded metal flooring, or abrasive coating on surfaces used for walking, climbing, or footholds shall be provided as appropriate.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Access to all serviceable points
text: Access shall be provided to all points, items, units, and components that require testing, servicing, adjusting, removing, replacing, and repairing.
site_hook: Reach from maintainer mannequin to each tagged service point

title: Access opening size and considerations
text: Access openings shall be large enough to accommodate hands, arms, and tools, and provide full visual access to the task area; type, size, shape and location (see 5.9) shall be based on: location/environment, frequency of use, tasks in the cavity, time, tools, workspace, clothing, access reach, visual requirements, packaging, mounting, hazards, and size/shape/weight/clearance of appendages, tools and units entering.
site_hook: Sandbox access opening vs hand/arm breadth (+glove) and tool envelope; line of sight through opening
percentile_rule: Fit P95 male hand/arm with handwear

title: Physical space accommodation for operation and maintenance
limits: multivariate accommodation (each sex): >= 90 (preferred 95) % of population
text: Unless otherwise specified, physical space shall be designed into equipment so that accessibility and accommodation for all operational and maintenance activities is provided for at least the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and females of the target user population.
site_hook: Clearance/reach checks over boundary mannequins of both sexes
percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females; univariate: central 95% of each sex (i.e. P2.5 female to P97.5 male)

title: Body postures for access per 5.10
text: Where tasks require various body postures, the access opening and physical space for these postures shall be provided in accordance with 5.10.
site_hook: Apply Figure 59/60 posture clearances

title: Maintenance from above or outside
text: Whenever possible, equipment design shall permit maintenance from above or outside rather than from underneath or inside.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Minimum space per person
limits: floor area per person: >= 0.4 m2 [[4 sq ft]]
text: Space of 0.4 square meters (4 square feet) per person minimum shall be provided for personnel and their clothing, PPE, tools and equipment, plus free space for required movements.
site_hook: Clear floor area of work zone divided by number of mannequins

title: Working space for removed large parts
text: When maintenance requires removing large internal parts, the working space shall accommodate the person(s), the removed component, and laydown area for the component, tools, or equipment.
site_hook: Box object (component) + mannequin footprint must fit in the clear area

title: Arm and hand access openings
text: Access openings shall be located and sized to permit required adjustment or handling; provide a view of the item manipulated; have dimensions in accordance with 5.10; allow clearance for the maintainer's hand, hand wear and clothing; have a shape clearing the equipment (protuberances, handles), body parts and tools; and be large enough to use tools and test equipment within the access cavity.
site_hook: Access opening object vs hand/forearm dimensions (+glove allowance) and tool size; line of sight through opening
percentile_rule: Fit P95 male hand breadth/forearm with handwear

title: Visual access and inspection
text: Openings shall provide visual access large enough to view all required information at the normal operating or maintenance position; items requiring visual inspection (e.g. hydraulic reservoirs, gauges) shall be visible without removing panels or other components.
site_hook: Line of sight from eye point through opening to tagged item

title: Visual access only: order of precedence
text: Where only visual access is required: a. opening with no cover (unless degrading performance); b. transparent window if dirt/moisture could be a problem; c. break-resistant glass if wear, heat or solvents would cause optical deterioration.
site_hook: Checklist item

title: Corridor width for traffic load
text: Corridor widths shall be designed for the peak traffic load expected, for traffic directions, and for the number of entrances and exits in the area.
site_hook: Checklist; widths in Figure 77.

title: Corridor width - one person non-egress passage
limits: corridor clear width, one person passage: >= 510 (preferred 760) mm [non-egress]
text: One person non-egress passage forward: minimum 510 mm (20 in), preferred 760 mm (30 in) (5.11.3.1.2, corridors shall meet figure 77).
site_hook: New corridor object (or distance between two wall objects); compare width with min/pref and with clothed P95/P99 mannequin maximum body breadth.

title: Corridor width - two person passage
limits: corridor clear width, two person passage: 1.22-1.37 m
text: Two person passage: 1.22 - 1.37 m (4.0 - 4.5 ft).
site_hook: Corridor object width.

title: Corridor width - with one door opening into it
limits: corridor width with one door: 1.67-1.83 m
text: Corridor with one door (swinging into corridor): 1.67 - 1.83 m (5.5 - 6.0 ft).
site_hook: Corridor object width + door object on corridor wall.

title: Corridor width - facing doors
limits: corridor width with facing doors: 2.13-2.34 m
text: Corridor with facing doors: 2.13 - 2.34 m (7.0 - 7.7 ft).
site_hook: Corridor object width + two facing door objects.

title: Corridor clearance for bulky clothing
limits: corridor width, one person in bulky clothing: >= 760 mm | corridor width passable with some difficulty: >= 510 mm [info]
text: Clearance should be allowed for personnel wearing bulky clothing and carrying equipment. A person can move through a corridor 510 mm (20 in) wide with some difficulty; a corridor for one person to travel comfortably even in bulky clothes should be at least 760 mm (30 in) wide. Carried equipment may add width.
site_hook: Corridor width vs mannequin max breadth (bideltoid/hip) + clothing allowance + carried box width.

title: Wheelchair accessible route width
limits: accessible route clear width, single wheelchair: >= 915 mm | clear width at doors / short constriction: >= 815 mm [constriction length max 610 mm (24 in) per figure 78]
text: The minimum clear width of an accessible route for a single wheelchair shall be 915 mm (36 in) except at doors, which shall be 815 mm (32 in) (figure 78). Figure 78 shows the 815 mm (32 in) minimum applies over a 610 mm (24 in) max. distance for min. clearance.
site_hook: Corridor/route object width and door clear width; wheelchair occupant not modelled.

title: Width for two wheelchairs to pass
limits: route clear width for two wheelchairs: >= 1525 mm
text: The minimum width for two wheelchairs to pass shall be 1,525 mm (60 in) (figure 79).
site_hook: Corridor object width.

title: Wheelchair passing spaces
limits: passing space size: >= 1525 mm [square, each side] | interval between passing spaces: <= 61 m
text: If an accessible route has less than 1,525 mm (60 in) clear width, passing spaces at least 1,525 by 1,525 mm (60 by 60 in) shall be located at reasonable intervals not to exceed 61 m (200 ft).
site_hook: Route layout; manual entry.

title: Accessible routes from site arrival points
text: At least one accessible route within the site boundary shall be provided from public transportation stops, accessible parking, passenger unloading zones, and public streets or sidewalks to the accessible building entrance; at least one accessible route shall connect accessible buildings, facilities, elements and spaces on the same site (5.11.3.2.7) and connect accessible entrances with all accessible spaces within the building (5.11.3.2.8).
site_hook: Checklist.

title: Accessible route excludes stairs/escalators
text: An accessible route shall not include stairs, steps, or escalators.
site_hook: Checklist (could flag stair objects placed on a route tagged accessible).

title: Accessible route as emergency exit
text: Accessible routes serving any accessible space or element shall also serve as a means of exit for emergencies or connect to an accessible area of rescue assistance.
site_hook: Checklist.

title: Accessible route 90-degree turn widths
limits: route clear width at 90-degree turn, each leg: >= 915 mm [obstruction width >= 1220 mm (48 in)] | width of obstruction for 915 mm legs to apply: >= 1220 mm
text: If a wheelchair user must turn around an obstruction, the minimum clear width shall be as shown on figures 80 and 81 (5.11.3.2.9). Figure 80 (90-degree turn): each leg 915 mm min. (36 in); obstruction (inside corner) width 1220 mm min. (48 in).
site_hook: Route/corridor geometry.

title: Accessible route 180-degree turn around obstruction
limits: route clear width each leg at U-turn: >= 1065 mm [obstruction width x < 1220 mm (48 in)] | clear depth beyond end of obstruction: >= 1220 mm [x < 1220 mm]
text: Figure 81 (turn around an obstruction narrower than 1220 mm (48 in), x < 1220 mm): each leg 1065 mm min. (42 in); clear depth at the turn 1220 mm min. (48 in).
site_hook: Route/corridor geometry.

title: Protruding objects not reduce clear width
text: Protruding objects shall not reduce the clear width of an accessible route or a maneuvering space.
site_hook: Objects intruding into a corridor object's clear width.

title: Changes in level on accessible routes
limits: vertical change in level without treatment: <= 6 mm | beveled change in level (bevel slope max 1:2): 6-13 mm | change in level requiring ramp: >= 13 mm [greater than 13 mm]
text: Changes in level up to 6 mm (0.25 in) may be vertical without edge treatment; from 6 to 13 mm (0.25 to 0.5 in) shall be beveled with a slope no greater than 1:2; greater than 13 mm (0.5 in) shall be accomplished by a ramp.
site_hook: Step/threshold height on a route; user entry or stair object with 1 step.

title: Carpet pile height
limits: carpet pile height: <= 13 mm
text: Carpet pile height shall be a maximum of 13 mm (0.5 in); carpet securely attached with firm pad or no pad (5.11.3.2.12.1); exposed edges fastened with trim along the entire length (5.11.3.2.12.2).
site_hook: Checklist / user entry.

title: Running slope above 1:20 is a ramp
limits: running slope of accessible route (not a ramp): <= 0.05 ratio (rise/run) [printed as 1:20]
text: An accessible route with a running slope greater than 1:20 is considered a ramp and shall comply with 5.11.8.2.
site_hook: Slope of ramp/route object.

title: Maximum cross slope
limits: cross slope of accessible route: <= 0.02 ratio (rise/run) [printed as 1:50]
text: Nowhere shall the cross slope of an accessible route exceed 1:50.
site_hook: Route object cross slope.

title: Clear width of doors (accessible)
limits: door clear opening width at 90 degrees open: >= 815 mm
text: Doorways shall have a minimum clear opening of 815 mm (32 in) with the door open 90 degrees, measured between the face of the door and the opposite doorstop.
site_hook: Sandbox door width (clear opening = leaf width minus door thickness/stops).

title: Floors stable, firm, slip resistant
text: Floors shall be stable, firm, and slip resistant; walkway surfaces shall be stable, planar, flush, and even to the maximum extent possible (5.11.4.2).
site_hook: Checklist.

title: Non-skid walkway surfaces
text: Walkway surfaces used for ammunition handling or movement of stores (5.11.4.3.1), and walkways reasonably anticipated to be exposed to water, condensation, or other liquids (5.11.4.3.2), shall have non-skid surfaces on all areas where personnel walk or stand to work.
site_hook: Checklist.

title: Catwalks/tunnels/crawl spaces accommodate operations
text: Catwalks, tunnels, and crawl spaces shall be designed to ensure personnel safety (see 5.7.7.2), accommodate operations performed therein, and accommodate personnel clothing and equipment.
site_hook: Clearance of clothed mannequin within tunnel/catwalk object.

title: Minimum catwalk width
limits: catwalk floor width: >= 460 mm
text: The minimum catwalk floor width shall be 460 mm (18 in) to accommodate walking one foot in front of the other and carrying tools or equipment.
site_hook: New catwalk/platform object width.

title: Ventilation of enclosed catwalks/tunnels/crawl spaces
text: Enclosed catwalks, tunnels, and crawl spaces shall have air ventilation to sustain their maximum permissible personnel numbers indefinitely; temperature and air quality shall be considered.
site_hook: Not geometric.

title: Tunnel/crawl space body clearance (multivariate largest 99 %)
text: When tunnels or crawl spaces require bending, stooping, or crawling, they shall accommodate the multivariate largest 99 percent of the male and the multivariate largest 99 percent of the female target user population to accomplish movement and, where applicable, work without mechanical aids.
site_hook: New tunnel/crawl-space box object (height, width); place P99 male and P99 female mannequins in crawling/kneeling/stooping postures and check collision/clearance (use multivariate cases if available).
percentile_rule: accommodate multivariate largest 99 % of male and of female target population

title: Use platforms to raise personnel to working distance
text: Platforms should be used where personnel must be raised to the working distance of equipment; guardrails shall be provided in accordance with 5.11.6.3 (5.11.6.1.1).
site_hook: Reach from standing mannequin to target; suggest platform height if out of reach.

title: Platform minimum dimensions
limits: platform width: >= 610 mm | platform length: >= 910 mm
text: Platforms shall measure at least 610 mm (24 in) wide by 910 mm (36 in) long.
site_hook: New platform object (or box used as platform) width/length.

title: Hands-free work on platform
text: Platform design shall permit both of the user's hands to be free for work.
site_hook: Checklist (posture without hand support).

title: Gap between platform and equipment
limits: gap between platform edge and equipment: <= 150 (preferred 50) mm [preferred: within 50 mm]
text: Platform design shall not have gaps greater than 150 mm (6 in) between the equipment and the platform; the preferred gap is within 50 mm (2 in).
site_hook: Point-to-point distance between platform edge and equipment object.

title: Protect equipment surfaces from platform
text: Contact plates, cushions, bumpers, or pads shall be used, as necessary, to protect equipment surfaces.
site_hook: Checklist.

title: Platform strength (113.4 kg per person)
limits: design personnel weight per person: >= 113.4 kg
text: The platform shall hold the worker(s) plus the heaviest tools and equipment expected plus a safety factor; use 113.4 kg (250 lb) per person to estimate personnel weight.
site_hook: Platform load rating entered by user vs persons x 113.4 kg + tool masses.

title: Test equipment support height on platform
text: When test equipment will be used, the design shall provide support for test equipment at the appropriate height for its use.
site_hook: Shelf/table object height vs mannequin elbow/eye height on platform.

title: Platform surfaces: grating / non-skid
text: Exterior platforms and similar work areas shall be constructed of open metal grating; where grating is impractical, and for interior platforms and passageways, floor surfaces shall be treated with non-skid material (5.11.6.1.9).
site_hook: Checklist.

title: Portable platforms
text: Portable platforms should be lightweight and fully collapsible; any platform on wheels shall have brakes and wheel locks (5.11.6.2.2).
site_hook: Checklist.

title: Guardrails with two rails on open sides
limits: number of rails on open sides: >= 2 count
text: All open sides of personnel platforms shall be equipped with guardrails that have at least two rails (an intermediate rail and top rail).
site_hook: Platform object with rail count per side.

title: Guardrail top rail height
limits: top rail height above platform: >= 1.1 m
text: Top rail height shall be not less than 1.1 m (42 in).
site_hook: Rail object height above platform surface; compare with mannequin COM height.

title: Guardrail setback from platform edge
limits: platform edge to rail centerline distance: <= 65 mm
text: Distance between the platform edge and the centerline of the railing shall be not greater than 65 mm (2.5 in).
site_hook: Distance between rail object and platform edge.

title: Guardrail rail diameter
limits: guardrail diameter: 37-75 mm
text: Rail diameter is between 37 mm (1.5 in) and 75 mm (3 in).
site_hook: Rail/grab-bar diameter parameter.

title: Toe board / guard screen height
limits: toe board or guard screen height: >= 150 mm
text: The height of a toe board or guard screen shall be not less than 150 mm (6 in).
site_hook: Add toe-board parameter to platform object.

title: Platform handholds
text: Handholds shall be furnished where needed to assist in climbing onto a platform or as aids in performing maintenance tasks; and shall be provided (with guardrails) where personnel must stabilize themselves due to wind, ice, fog, other hazards or moving vehicles (5.11.6.3.5).
site_hook: Grab-bar placement within reach of climbing/standing mannequin.

title: Elevator/lift operating safety features
text: Where elevators, inclinators, or hydraulic work platforms are needed: maximum load signs easily seen; guards against accidental operation; easily reachable manual lowering capability when feasible; floor surface treatment per 5.11.6.1.9.
