site_hook: Checklist; manual-lowering control reach could be checked with hand-reach tool.

title: Means of exit continuity
text: The exit path shall not be interrupted by any building element other than an exit component (e.g., a ramp).
site_hook: Checklist.

title: Conventional entrances for enclosed work areas
text: Enclosed work areas should have conventional entrances and exits for routine access and unrestricted flow of traffic and equipment; located so personnel entering/leaving will not inadvertently operate or block controls or displays or interfere with ongoing work (5.11.7.1.3).
site_hook: Distance from door swing / entry path to control and display objects.

title: Exit illumination level

text: The illumination level of an exit shall be not less than 11 lux (1 foot-candle) at the walking surface.
site_hook: User-entered illuminance.

title: Hinged door clear width

site_hook: Sandbox door width; also compare with clothed P99 max body breadth.

title: Hinged door height
limits: door height: 2.0-2.1 m
text: Door height 2.0 - 2.1 m (6.6 - 6.9 ft).
site_hook: Sandbox door height; also compare with P99 stature + footwear/helmet.

title: Door hinge-side clearance to wall

text: Figure 82 shows 100 - 300 mm (4 - 12 in) between the door at the hinge side and the perpendicular wall.
site_hook: Distance from door hinge edge to adjacent wall object.

title: Side-hinged doors in exit routes

site_hook: Checklist.

title: Inward door clearance to perpendicular wall

title: Equipment clear of inward door swing

title: Door opening direction by traffic density

site_hook: Checklist.

title: Emergency exit space for occupants with equipment
text: Emergency exits shall allow enough space for rapid exit of all occupants, including any who carry essential equipment or wear bulky clothing, without injury or equipment damage (29 CFR 1910.36, 1910.37, NFPA).

title: Emergency exit design criteria (qualitative)
text: Emergency doors and exits shall be simple to operate, readily accessible, clearly designated, unobstructed, simple to locate and operate in the dark, and not in themselves constitute a safety hazard.

title: Emergency exit egress time per person

text: Emergency doors and exits shall permit exit by one person in 5 seconds or less (item h).
site_hook: User-entered test time.

title: Lifting limits - scope and exclusions
limits: object mass for lifting limits to apply: >= 2.3 kg [5 lb; limits apply above this] | holding duration within scope: <= 3 s [holding > 3 s out of scope] | lifting shift duration within scope: <= 8 h [> 8 h out of scope] | lifting speed within scope: <= 75 cm/s [30 in/s; faster is out of scope] | sole-floor coefficient of friction within scope: >= 0.4 - [< 0.4 slippery = out of scope] | ambient temperature within scope: 19-26 degC [66 to 79 degF]
text: Lifting limits depend on posture relative to load, frequency and duration. Unless otherwise specified they accommodate the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of clothed/equipped males and females of the target population. They do NOT apply to: lifting outside a stationary location, holding more than 3 seconds, one-handed lifting, lifting with hands and other body parts (shoulder or leg), lifting more than 8 hours, lifting seated or kneeling, restricted space, unstable surface, while operating equipment, high speed (faster than 75 cm/s [30 in/s]), slippery floors (<0.4 coefficient of friction sole-floor), and cold or hot environments (outside temperature 19 to 26 degC [66 to 79 degF]). Generally not applicable to unbalanced load or posture (biomechanical analysis recommended). The limits apply to objects that weigh more than 2.3 kg (5 lb).
site_hook: Lifting calculator should validate inputs: two-handed, standing (not seated/kneeling), mass > 2.3 kg, speed <= 75 cm/s, COF >= 0.4, temp 19-26 degC, else warn 'outside NIOSH scope'.

title: Lifting equation (maximum weight limit WL)
limits: load constant LC: <= 23 kg [51 lb]
text: WL = LC x HM x VM x DM x AM x FM x CM, where LC (load constant) = 23 kg (51 lb), HM horizontal multiplier, VM vertical multiplier, DM distance multiplier, AM asymmetry multiplier, FM frequency multiplier (table XLV), CM coupling multiplier (table XLVI). In the ideal lifting condition all multipliers are 1.0; otherwise multipliers < 1.0 reduce WL.
site_hook: Implement in posture analysis for lifting postures: H, V from hand/box CG vs mid-point between inner ankle bones; D from origin/destination V; A from trunk-to-load angle; F, duration, coupling entered by user; compare box mass to min(WL_origin, WL_destination).
percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

title: Formulas for lifting multipliers
limits: HM: <= 1.0 - [metric: 25/H (H in cm); customary: 10/H (H in in)] | VM: <= 1.0 - [metric: 1-(0.003*|V-75|) (V in cm); customary: 1-(0.0075*|V-30|)] | DM: <= 1.0 - [metric: 0.82+(4.5/D) (D in cm); customary: 0.82+(1.8/D)] | AM: <= 1.0 - [1-(0.0032*A), A in degrees (both unit systems)] | FM: <= 1.0 - [lookup table XLV] | CM: <= 1.0 - [lookup table XLVI]
text: Metric (cm): HM = 25/H; VM = 1 - (0.003|V-75|); DM = 0.82 + (4.5/D); AM = 1 - (0.0032A) (A in degrees); FM from table XLV; CM from table XLVI. US customary (in): HM = 10/H; VM = 1 - (0.0075|V-30|); DM = 0.82 + (1.8/D); AM = 1 - (0.0032A). Notes: sourced from Applications Manual for the Revised NIOSH Lifting Equation; multipliers may not exceed 1.0 - values > 1.0 are set to 1.0 (e.g., D = 10 cm gives 0.82+(4.5/10) = 1.27, so DM = 1.0).
site_hook: Clamp each multiplier to max 1.0. NOTE: Table XLII prints no lower cut-offs for H, V, D, A (the NIOSH manual uses H 25-63 cm, V 0-175 cm, D 25-175 cm, A 0-135 deg) - site should not invent them, but may warn that values outside NIOSH ranges are unvalidated.

title: Definitions of lifting task variables (H, V, D, A)
text: H = distance between the floor projection of the load CG and the projection of the person's CG (figures 98/99: measured from the mid-point between the inner ankle bones to the point of projection of the load). V = vertical distance from load CG to the floor. D = vertical travel distance between origin and destination. A = angular displacement of the load from the sagittal line (asymmetry angle between sagittal line and asymmetry line, figure 99).
site_hook: Geometry: H = horizontal distance (top view) from midpoint of inner ankle bones to box CG projection; V = box CG height above floor; A = angle between mannequin sagittal line and line from ankle midpoint to load projection.

title: Evaluate lift at origin and destination

site_hook: Compute WL for both lift-origin and lift-destination postures; report min.

title: Graphic representation of task variables H and V

site_hook: Reference geometry for H and V measurement.

title: Graphic representation of task variable A

site_hook: Reference geometry for A measurement.

title: Lifting duration categories

title: Lifting duration category and required rest

text: Short: t <= 1 hour, required resting period >=100% of duration of continuous lifting task. Moderate: 1 hour < t <= 2 hours, >=30% of continuous lifting task. title: Frequency multiplier inputs and 15 lifts/min cap

Limits may be reduced when body armor/worn equipment exceeds 9 kg (20 lb); if load carriage weighs more than 9 kg (20 lb), a biomechanical analysis and energy expenditure estimation shall be performed. Lifting limits at the origin (before carrying) and destination (after carrying) shall be determined, and the lowest of the three limits used.
